newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London saw another lacklustre trading day in the absence of the raws market as the March/May spread dominated the little activity seen. Ranges were confined to a maximum of 80 cents and the spot March contract was reluctant to test initial resistance at $305.30 per tonne. The March/May spread attracted commission house buying at level money, while outright trade and commission purchases were also seen in March. At the close the spread had barely moved from its opening level and stood at a narrow 10 cents. March was up 20 cents at $303.90 and May down 30 cents at $304.00. The New York market was closed for the Thanksgiving holiday.

NETHERLANDS - Sugar imports in August 1996 amounted to 1,951 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 3,993 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first 11 months of 1995/96 (October/August) up to 54,357 tonnes compared to 51,810 imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 64,568 tonnes compared to 79,854 tonnes in 1993/94 and 110,824 tonnes in 1992/93. Major countries of origin in October/August 1995/96 were France with 20,026 tonnes whites against 16,760 tonnes and Belgium- Luxembourg with 17,108 tonnes, up from 14,473 tonnes. Sugar exports in August 1996 reached 7,435 tonnes, sharply down from last year's 14,593 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in October/August 1995/96 up to 295,571 tonnes against 376,481 tonnes in October/August 1994/95. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 381,586 tonnes compared to 654,277 tonnes in 1993/94 and 439,641 tonnes in 1992/93. Major countries of destination in October/August 1995/96 were Iran with 61,805 tonnes whites against 90,805 tonnes, Libya with 31,577 tonnes compared to 21 tonnes and Turkey with 23,925 tonnes, down from 28,816 tonnes.

MEXICO - Sugar yields and a lower quantity of cane milled are plaguing the Mexican sugar campaign which has started in early November. The total amount of cane milled up to November 23 was 302,116 tonnes, sharply down from last year's 806,736 tonnes. Sugar output so far reached 21,905 tonnes compared to 57,771 tonnes in 1995/96 and 35,968 tonnes in 1994/95. The sugar yield in the week ended November 23 was 7.42 per cent, down from 7.53 per cent in 1995/96 and 8.13 per cent in 1994/95.

SPAIN - Sugar imports in August 1996 reached 45,384 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 16,327 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first two months of 1996/97 (July/August) up to 83,247 tonnes against 44,886 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 353,193 tonnes against 257,273 tonnes in 1994/95 and 252,750 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in July/August 1996/97 were France with 57,650 tonnes whites against 26,644 tonnes and Germany with 6,768 tonnes, down from 10,345 tonnes. Sugar exports in August 1996 amounted to 11,829 tonnes, down from 31,315 tonnes in August 1995. This brought cumulative exports in July/August 1996 up to 22,622 tonnes against 72,970 in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 208,130 tonnes against 195,960 in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in July/August 1996 were Tunisia with 9,150 tonnes whites against 15,141 tonnes and Senegal with 5,380 tonnes compared to 2 tonnes.
Iran was said to have bought a cargo of 45 ICUMSA whites at $312.50 per tonne for March shipment as part of its seasonal buying programme. Further details were not immediately available.
